source: Rich Mix public Spektrix v3 API (no credentials, no auth headers)

requests.reduction: REDUCED from 354 events (262 FILM) to 40 (31 FILM): every event referenced by a future instance, plus 30 FILM controls that have no future instance. The subset preserves the shape that matters — a populated film catalogue against an almost empty film calendar. sha256 above is of the FULL 387 KB response, not committed.
No records removed; JSON pretty-printed for the fixture. bytes and sha256 above describe the original compact response. Compact serialization of the fixture reproduces that original hash.

note: instances.json is the complete response body that endpoint returned for that query. The endpoint's contract is established from vendor documentation (see endpointContract), which documents v3/instances as returning all instances matching the query with no pagination mechanism. Absent Link/Content-Range headers and a matching content-length corroborate that we received the whole body; on their own they would prove only that.
scopeLimit: A 2026-09-09 observation. It does NOT establish what the source held on 2026-09-08, so it cannot show the baseline run's extraction was correct or incorrect. It also does not establish a cause for the low film denominator. The latest instance among six sampled catalogue films was 2026-08-27; a different FILM event in the captured instances response has a 2026-09-09 screening.
paginationContractVerified: yes, against vendor documentation (no pagination mechanism documented); not verified by measurement

independentDiscoveryCheck.why: Six per-event API samples cannot rule out the venue having moved its film programme to a different publishing route. This check uses a route independent of the Spektrix API.
independentDiscoveryCheck.sitemapGeneratedAt: 2026-09-09T20:15:49+01:00 (19:15:49Z, approximately one hour before the recorded fetch)
independentDiscoveryCheck.result: 53 URLs. Exactly ONE /cinema/<detail> page: https://richmix.org.uk/cinema/premiere-we-set-the-house-on-fire — the same single film the Spektrix API returned. Also 7 /live-events/<detail> pages, consistent with the API's 9 LIVE instances.
independentDiscoveryCheck.establishes: The venue's sitemap listed one cinema detail page at capture time, corroborating the single film the API returned.
independentDiscoveryCheck.doesNotEstablish: That the website is not advertising a programme the API misses. A sitemap is a CMS-generated index and need not enumerate everything a site publishes — sections can be omitted, stale, or rendered without dedicated detail pages. This is corroboration from a second route, not proof of absence. The /cinema/ listing page is client-rendered via Spektrix web components and server-returns no showtimes, so it could not be counted directly without a browser. No cause is established and no other publishing route is ruled out.

endpointContract.summary: The vendor describes v3/instances as a collection of instances filtered by supported query parameters and recommends bounded dates to limit response size. Supported filters include startFrom, startTo, eventName and event/instance attributes.
endpointContract.reading: The collection endpoint is documented to return ALL instances matching the query, with no pagination mechanism described — the stated caveat is response SIZE, not truncation. So `?startFrom=<today>` is documented to return every future instance. This, not the absence of Link/Content-Range headers, is what establishes the contract; the header observation is corroboration only.
endpointContract.perEventNote: Our /events/{id}/instances probes passed no parameters, so they returned each event's full instance history (108 and 123 rows, all past), which is what we observed. Note the docs use a different parameter form elsewhere, v3/events?instanceStart_from/instanceStart_to.
endpointContract.residual: Documentation is a vendor statement, not a measurement. It is a materially better basis than header absence, and it is still not a proof about this tenant's data.
